findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair:

1. The front handwashing sink is observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 
2. There is a leak in the bottom corners of the walk-in cooler door that is creating mold accumulation. Ensure that this issue is repaired and the floor and walk-in cooler door are cleaned to remove the accumulation. 
3. There is a broken cove tile behind the standing freezer by the first drive-through window. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled during inspection. 
1. The nozzle of the soda machine was observed to be soiled. 
2. Inspector observed soil accumulation on the internal surface of other coffee maker.
PIC was made aware. PIC instructed a staff member to clean and sanitize the above mentioned food contact surfaces. Inspector reexamined the surfaces mention and they appeared to have been cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda machine nozzle and the internal surface of the coffee maker are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized on a regular basis.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.16(B) The following spaces in the wall juncture were observed to not be sealed.
1. Inspector observed a broken cove tile on the right side of the entrance of the walk-in cooler behind the shelving.
2. A broken cove tile was observed behind the standing freezer by the first drive-thru window.

PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the broken tile will be sealed properly. Ensure that these tiles are replaced and sealed to the wall appropriately to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.  

 Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 The gasket on the door of the walk-in cooler was observed to be coming off. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that the gasket had already arrived at the facility. The gasket will be installed in a timely manner. Ensure that these tiles gasket is replaced and sealed to the door. 


Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

A container of pre-cooked chicken is observed in the bottom of the cooler next to the back chili steam well with internal temperatures of 55F. The PIC was shown and stated that it was placed in the cooler this morning. The chicken was discarded to correct. Per the PIC this cooler will no longer be used for storing of TCS foods. They also stated that it normally only holds clean trays/pans. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored so that they maintain temperatures of 41F or less at all times.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of grease on the sides of the fryers, the floor under the fryers, the wall behind the fryers, and on the hood system above the fryers. The drips forming on the hood system above the fryers pose the risk of contaminating food cooking underneath. The PIC was instructed to clean around, underneath, and above the fryers at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are kept free of grease deposits and other soil accumulations by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking 
EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the unused cooler across from the ice machine has an accumulation of food debris inside. The PIC was educated that equipment (even those currently not being used) must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food debris. The inside of the cooler was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are kept free of accumulations of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there are holes in the wall above the mop sink and the ice machine that must be sealed. The holes can be sealed using caulking or another method that creates smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: 2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee wash hands and turn off the faucet with bare hands. The employee stated that turning off the faucet handle with a towel was stupid. The employee was coached on proper hand washing and the reason why a clean barrier is needed between clean hands and the dirty faucet handle. Ensure that hand washing is coached on a regular basis. Employee washed hands twice during the coaching. The violation was corrected on site. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Inspector observed the lids on the burger cooler to be soiled with meat debris and crumbs. The soiled lids were exchanged for clean lids. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Foods in the Henny Penny were cold. The bottom shelf was not even turned on. Chicken items were between 98F and 130F when temperature checked with a probe thermometer. The items were voluntarily discarded.

(A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: The cold holding unit under the sandwich line on lobby side is dripping. The other side is not able to push the cold air over to the condiment holding area. The condiment holding area shall not be used until the problem can be identified and fixed. The refrigeration professional will propose a solution. 
The sandwich area of the make table is holding as long as the food is not more than half full in the pans of the unit. Ensure that pans are not stocked too high. Take temperatures regularly. 
After a discussion with the manager on duty. The facility is going to discontinue use of that counter top cold holding area. A spot check will be conducted. 
EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.comment:
2-303.11: Inspector observed an employee with multiple cloth bracelets on their wrist. Ensure that employees hands and wrists are free of jewelry. The employee was heading home and clocked out. 

Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing FOOD, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.comment:
2-402.11:  Inspectors observed two male employees to be lacking hair restraints. Ensure that employees wear proper hair restraints in the food service facility while doing food preparation activities. 

 (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wear hair restraints designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed FOOD. (B) Section is not applicable to FOOD EMPLOYEES who only serve BEVERAGES and wrapped or PACKAGED FOODS, hostesses, and wait staff if they present minimal RISK.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.comment:
2-304.11: The inspector observed employee with a soiled uniform shirt on. The shirt was soiled with water from washing dishes. She changed her shirt. The inspector discussed clean uniforms  and the use of aprons as needed to keep uniforms clean. The facility has extra shirts of all sized so that employees can change as needed. 

2-304.11: Food employees shall wear clean outer clothing to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service and single-use articles.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee wash hands, turn off the faucet with a towel and then continue to wipe hands with that same towel before disposing of the towel in the garbage. Ensure that hand washing is coached on a regular basis. Employee was coached immediately by inspector and washed hands correctly. The violation was corrected on site. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the area around fry station to be soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil for the next routine inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Salads under the make table in the holding area are between 45F and 48F. The internal thermometer reads 45 and the digital thermometer on the side of the unit reads 46F. The unit can not go through defrost during times of peak use. The grill line make table has gone up 10 degrees in the past 4 hours according to employee. He checked the unit  and it was 36F when he started work at 9am. They are moving the food back to the lobby side and will not use the unit until it is verified to be holding at a temperature that can maintain food 41F or below. Salads will be served until 3pm which is 6 hours form the time they were prepared. Any salads that remain will be discarded in the garbage. They are working on making new salads and will hold them wither in the lobby side or in the walk in unit.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The unit no longer has the capacity to maintain food at 41F or below under conditions of normal use. Repair the unit to maintain food at 41F or below at all times. Do not use the unit until it can maintain. Call to verify the ability of the unit before use. 
Please contact the Department if more time is needed to properly repair the unit.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Two Priority items are observed to be out of compliance at the time of inspection. It would be beneficial to keep temperature logs on all units. At a minimum this would be done one time per day. Ideally this would be done more often. Every four hours during hours of operation is reasonable. 
Management was coached at time of inspection on proactive management techniques (such as keeping temperature logs). The violation is considered corrected at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Chicken nuggets at the fry hot holding area are 120F when probed internally. The Nuggets were discarded in the garbage and fresh nuggets put down. Follow corporate policy on discarding nuggets when timer sounds.  Violation is considered corrected at this time.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The sandwich table reach in cooler at drive up side is holding 30 salads. The table internal thermometer reads 48F. The sandwich prep top is marginal at 43F to 45F. The lobby side is working. Sandwich prep has been moved to the lobby side. The management has called to have the unit evaluated and repaired as needed. The salads were discarded in the garbage. The violation is considered corrected as they have a second, identical side to work out of. A spot check will be conducted on 6/27/23 to ensure that the unit is either working or is not being used.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Soil is observed around/under the fryers and at the floor drain for the 3 part sink. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil. Clean sides of floor drain also.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed handle of cheese scoop to be touching the food. Scoop was removed and placed with handle out of the food with lid propped open. Store handled scoops properly.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.comment:
3-304.15: (A) SIGLE-USE  gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with ready to. Eat food or with raw animal food, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.(P)

Observed the sandwich prep worker to adjust clothing. He was stopped and asked coached about keeping gloves clean. He washed hands properly and changed gloves. Take every opportunity to train single-use glove use and hand washing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines. 

Observed the front hand sink to lack water - sensor is not turning on water. PIC has repair call for service. Inspector will follow-up regarding hot water status on 6/14/21. Facility should utilize back hand sink near three compartment sink until front hand sink is repaired.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed mop to be stored improperly between uses. Hang in a manner that allows to air or drip dry. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at various sanitizer buckets. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114

Observed 3 sanitization buckets to be at 100 ppm concentration of quat. The 4th sani bucket registered within guidelines, 200 ppm. Advised PIC to change buckets during inspection. Discussed with PIC to ensure all sani buckets remain between 200 to 400 ppm and to routinely test and/or change out solution. COS.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Tongs (food contact surface) is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed multiple tongs utilized for hot holding to be soiled with food residue. Discussed how often tongs are washed, rinsed, and sanitized with PIC. PIC indicated twice a day. Discussed wash, rinse, and sanitizing tongs every 4 hours with PIC (food contact surface). COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink to have an accumulation of debris. Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces with PIC. This is a repeat violation since previous routine inspection on 10/22/19.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Caulk at 3 compartment sink was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulk to be peeling away at 3 compartment sink. Discussed re-caulking repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on 3 compartment sink spray nozzle. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-304.11  (P) Observed the nozzle for the fountain drink machine in the front of the store to have a slimy of white substance between the fins. The item was cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Multiple plastic pans were observed with accumulated grime in the creases around the edges. PIC was notified and the items were moved for detailed cleaning during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Bacon was observed at 78 degrees in a steam table that was not turned on. The bacon is not crispy by the inspector's opinion. A discussion with the PIC revealed the items were likely placed in the steam table around 11 AM that morning. The bacon was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) Approximately a dozen flies were observed in the kitchen area. Some are near the dish area, some are around the grill, some are by the mop sink and the last ones are by the cash register area. PIC was instructed to consult their pest control agency for more effective control methods. Follow up will take place in 2 weeks.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 All CFPMs in the facility are required to complete an ANSI accredited allergen course. At this time only one at the facility has done so. PIC was instructed to ensure that each CFPM completes a required course.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The following items were found cold holding above 41F:

In the SW preparation line cold holding well (only used for lunch):
(TOP): large peices of iceberg lettuce 55F, small chopped iceberg lettuce 52F, baby spinach 54F, asiago cheese 55F, shredded cheddar 57F, muenster cheese slices 56F. Ambient temperature of top portion of unit 47F-49F. Ambient temperature of bottom portion 39F-44F.  (BOTTOM): taco salads 44F in lidded clam shell containers, staff indicated items were prepped the morning of inspection. Discussed opening clam shells to allow food to cool more rapid. (PHF items were transferred into ice baths, PIC has called maintenance to repair cooler to hold below 41F)

In the walk-in cooler:
Iceberg lettuce 60F found stacked deeply in large plastic, lidded container. Staff indicated item was prepped less than 3 hours to inspection. Lettuce was transferred into smaller containers with ice baths for rapid cooling. 
2 bins of cut lettuce and romaine greens 44F found in lidded plastic bins. Lettuce was prepped the morning of inspection. Lids were removed for rapid cooling.

->Cold held food items must be maintained with temperatures less than 41F. Cold holding units are to be repaired and maintained to hold below 41F for safe food holding. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
The sprayer hose at the 3 compartment sink was noted extending into the basin of the sink and below the flood rim.

->The water supply inlet is below the flood rim of the fixture/equipment. Provide an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet or at least 1 inch. Reference 5-202.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following floors were found soiled with grease, grime, and debris at the time of inspection:
floors underneath the 3 compartment sink, underneath the soda syrup shelf, and in the room with the mop sink. Please clean and maintain. 

->Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed cheese sauce sitting in the prep sink with no potable water. Follow proper thawing methods.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the coffee spout to be soiled in the drive thru area. Clean food contact surfaces as needed.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a small amount of food splash on the wall where the second warmer of chili sits near the three compartment sink. Clean the walls as needed.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed ice buildup in the walk in freezer. Clean the floors as needed.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed no time mark on the tomatoes. A time was provided and must be used within eight hours according to Wendy's guidelines.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed dressings that stated to keep refrigerated were 52 F. The dressings were discarded during the inspection.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed the walk in freezer to have frost buildup. Make sure the floor is a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 2) Observed no floor drain cover at the mop sink. Provide a floor drain cover.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed multiple personal items stored on the single service glove boxes. Personal items shall be stored separate from food. The items were pulled during the inspection.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed chemicals in the back stored above single use gloves. The gloves were pulled during the inspection. Nothing food related shall be stored underneath chemicals.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed an employee drink in the prep area with no lid and straw. The cup was discarded during the inspection.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the coffee spout soiled. Clean the coffee spout.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed waste water sitting in the mop bucket. Mop water must be dumped after each use.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the dump sink in the drive thru area needing caulked to the countertop. Caulk the sink. 2) Observed the gasket ripped at the walk in cooler. Repair the gasket.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the side of the oven to be heavily soiled with grease accumulation. Degrease the side of the oven. 2) Observed the inside of the microwave to be soiled. Clean the microwave.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed wastewater sitting in the mop bucket that had not been dumped since this morning. Make sure to dump wastewater after each use to prevent pest control.
750-1130(e) Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the kitchen upon the arrival of inspection. Paper towels were replaced during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed multiple drain flies and house flies within the facility. Use PCO frequently to reduce flies.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) (REPEAT) Observed a missing drain cover at the mop sink. Replace drain cover. 2) Observed the floor near the mopsink to be soiled with debris accumulation. Properly keep floors clean to reduce pests.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the nudo board just outside the walk in cooler to be in disrepair. Make the wall smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed mops stored incorrectly. Mops should be hung to dry or inverted to prevent pests.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: In process of replacing motors on window units

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory

Another option for potentially hazardous food is to use time as a health control.  A policy sheet was left at the facility.  Following the last routine inspection, time as a control was implemented and a policy was written.  This was not in practice at this inspection.  Either adjust the cooler or use the policy.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed unwashed tomatoes above ready to eat food in the walk in cooler.  Store unwashed produce below ready to eat food and above raw meat.  Corrected:  items in the cooler were rearranged.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed dried food on the can opener blade.  Clean and sanitize the blade.  The opener was removed for cleaning.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following to be soiled:  1.bottom shelf of the reach in freezer (food and ice), 2.holes in the stainless steel prep table (accumulation of soil).  Clean these items and maintain clean.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed water leaks 1.at the spray nozzle, 2.at the 3-compartment sink faucet, and 3.at the prep sink.  Repair the leaks.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil on the floor between the stove and the wall.  Clean the floor and maintain clean.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
A Food Service Sanitation Manager was not present at the facility during the inspection.  The current store manager has a certificate in ServeSafe.  He was instructed to request reciprocity from the state.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
The patty cooler is not holding food at 41F or less.  This problem was recognized prior to my arrival and the facility is using time as a control until the cooler is repaired.  A spot check will be conducted to verify the cooler was repaired.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed cheese, sliced tomatoes and cooked egg on the prep line at 51F.  Hold potentially hazardous food at 41F or less.  If using time as a control, mark the food to indicate the time it was removed from temperature control and provide written procedures.  The food was moved to the prep table from a cooler at 10am, per Manager.  The two containers of tomatoes were moved to a cooler.  Do not keep these items on the prep line past 2pm.  If any is left at 2pm, discard.
